processing: Fresh leaf is spread to cool, then fixed, straightened and shaped or rolled, dried, sorted and packed.
harvest_season: Very early spring: gardens usually open in the first ten days of February, and spring tea made before 10 March carries the name.
appearance_dry: Flat, straight and neat, a glossy jade green.
taste_profile: A rich chestnut aroma, with a fresh, smooth and sweet taste.

brewing.notes: General advice for flat, tender greens: use a glass or an open gaiwan and cooler water, which keeps the chestnut note clean.

vintage_note: A calendar tea: the name itself covers spring tea made before 10 March, so it is sold as the current year's first harvest and reaches the market weeks ahead of most Chinese greens. Drink it within the year; there is no reason to keep it longer.
description:
Yibin Zaocha, literally Yibin early tea, is defined by the date as much as by the leaf. Yibin, in southern Sichuan, has warm winters and an early spring, and its gardens usually start picking in early February, about 15 to 30 days ahead of the main tea regions elsewhere in Sichuan and in Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

The main cultivars are Zaobaijian No. 5 and Fuxuan No. 9. The leaf is cooled, fixed, straightened and shaped, then dried, which gives a flat, straight tea in a glossy green.

The cup is described as bright tender green with a strong chestnut aroma and a fresh, sweet taste. As with other tender greens, too much heat is the common mistake, so let the water cool and pour off in good time.

It is a registered geographical indication covering a wide area, and the name refers to a harvest window more than one workshop, so quality varies. Ask for the picking date, and be wary of anything sold as this tea with no season on the pack.
history:
Local accounts link Yibin's early season to a Tang text, the Shanfu Jingshou Lu, on Sichuan tea shipped east, though the passage is general and the connection to Yibin is a local reading.

The modern reputation is firmer. In the 1970s and 1980s Yibin was asked to supply early tea to the spring Canton Fair, and local accounts report a 1978 auction price of 12,000 US dollars a tonne. The name itself was formally proposed by Wu Fatian, head of the city's tea station, in a technical paper. China's agriculture ministry registered Yibin Zaocha as a geographical indication on 8 March 2010, and the city has also run an annual early tea festival since 2008.
